diagnosis: After 65 programs the gain is only $5\times10^{-9}$, essentially LP-polishing tolerance, because nearly every worker starts from the record and its trust-region LP/shakes fall back into the same basin. The image explains why: hundreds of pairs lie within a few $10^{-9}$ of the maximum, yet at $10^{-9}$ tolerance 50 of 95 points are rattlers and the rest have only 0--5, highly unequal contacts, with a fragmented contact graph and an anisotropic, centrally clumped PC projection. The missing structural property is a rigid, balanced, near-isostatic contact network---every point carrying a comparable number (order $2\cdot600/95\approx12$ at a few-$10^{-9}$ tolerance) of contacts, all row maxima equalised, an isotropic frame $X^{T}X\approx(95/13)I$, and a positive equilibrium stress---rather than a few hub pairs plus free points. Once the linearised active set is exhausted the LP cannot create new contacts or rebalance row maxima, so real improvement requires changing contact topology, symmetry, or basin under strict time caps rather than longer polishing.
